commandSets.name: KeypadLinc
notes: Earlier sources give ramp rates 0x00 through 0x1F as 9 minutes down to 0.1 second; the later ones make 0x01 8 minutes and 0x00 2 seconds.

Earlier sources, the Insteon Developer's Guide and the KeypadLinc Line Developer Notes give D14 of the reply as the trigger mask; later sources moved the trigger mask to query 0x08 and use D14 for the radio group mask.
The Insteon Developer's Guide sets selectors 0x08 through 0x0C one button at a time; other sources write the whole mask.
The KeypadLinc Line Developer Notes cover firmware 0x41 and later of subcategories 0x1B, 0x1C, 0x0F, 0x1E and 0x2C, and every firmware of 0x41 and 0x42.
In the 6-button layout, the On and Off buttons are group 1 and the four small buttons groups 3 through 6; in the 8-button layout, the buttons are groups 1 through 8.

With the load detached, group 9 controls the load: cmd1 0x19 with cmd2 0x00 reads its level, D11 of the extended Get reply holds the LEDs of groups 1 through 8, a group 1 On or Off sets the group 1 LEDs, and the LED mask Set sets the others.

To make buttons act as radio buttons, set both the on mask and the off mask of each button to the other buttons in the group, and link each button as a controller with an off-only link (on-level 0x00) to the devices the other buttons control.

notes: Subcategories 0x11 and 0x12 are the European and Australian and New Zealand versions, the 2732-432 and 2732-532.
The owner's manual gives subcategory 0x0A to the 2441ZTH, 0x11 to the 2732-432 and 0x12 to the 2732-532.

devices.description: A small dimmer module that installs at a light fixture or behind an existing wall switch. It adds Insteon remote dimming control without replacing the original switch.
devices.name: Micro Dimmer Switch Module
notes: HouseLinc lists the regional versions as the 2442-222, 2442-422 and 2442-522.

devices.description: A small on/off relay module that installs in a fixture box or behind an existing wall switch. It adds Insteon remote control to a light while keeping the original switch.
devices.name: Micro On/Off Switch Module
notes: HouseLinc lists the regional versions as the 2443-222, 2443-422 and 2443-522.

devices.name: Access Point
notes: Insteon later reused the model number 2443 for the Micro On/Off Module, whose identities are its own.
It doesn't relay X10.

devices.description: A small in-box module that controls 110 V motorized devices such as projection screens, shutters, and curtains. It supports several switch types and has adjustable open and close travel times.
devices.name: Micro Open/Close Module
Mini Remote - 4 Scene
notes: With its grouped flag set, each row's on and off buttons share a group, 1 to 4 from the top. Otherwise each button has its own group, 1 to 8, left to right and top to bottom.
It sleeps between button presses, so it hears commands only while awake.

devices.name: Mini Remote - 8 Scene
notes: Groups 1 and 2 are buttons B and A, 3 and 4 are D and C, 5 and 6 are F and E, and 7 and 8 are H and G.

devices.name: Mini Remote - Switch
notes: It sends group 1 as one on/off pair by default, and can be set to two scenes.

devices.description: A plug-in module with a low-voltage sensor input and a relay output. It connects alarm sensors, door strikes, garage door openers, and other contact-closure devices to an Insteon network.
devices.name: I/O Module
notes: 0x07/0x0D is the version that detects 50 or 60 Hz power; Insteon Device Categories (January 2014) lists it as model 2450, and HouseLinc as 2450-50-60.

devices.description: A dimmer module that mounts on a DIN rail in an electrical panel to dim and switch lighting circuits remotely. It supports adjustable brightness levels and ramp rates.
devices.name: Dimmer DIN Rail Module
notes: HouseLinc also lists its identity under 2252-222.

devices.description: A relay module that mounts on a DIN rail in an electrical panel to switch lighting circuits on and off remotely over Insteon.
devices.name: On/Off DIN Rail Module

devices.description: A plug-in module that lets a dimmable lamp be turned on and off and dimmed remotely. The lamp plugs into the module, which plugs into a wall outlet.
devices.name: Dimmer Plug
notes: Linking and unlinking modes time out after 4 minutes.
Setting the on-level to 0 turns on resume dim.
Versions before 3.6 support X10; load sense is supported from version 3.6.

The 2014 to 2016 owner's manuals print subcategory 0x37, which the DIN Rail Dimmer 2452 reports in Australia and New Zealand; Insteon Device Categories (January 2014) gives the 2457D2 only 0x01/0x0E. A later hardware revision may report 0x37.

devices.name: Toggle Dimmer Switch
notes: HouseLinc lists subcategory 0x1F for firmware 0x3A and later.

devices.name: Toggle On/Off Switch
notes: HouseLinc lists subcategory 0x1A for firmware 0x3A and later.

devices.description: An in-wall duplex outlet whose top receptacle can be dimmed and switched remotely over Insteon while the bottom receptacle stays always on. It controls plug-in lamps from Insteon keypads, remotes, or the Hub.
devices.name: Dimmer Outlet
2-Wire Dimmer Switch
notes: Needs no neutral wire.
Repeats RF but not powerline.

devices.name: In-Line Dimmer Module
notes: Linked by holding SET for 10 seconds.

devices.name: In-Line Dimmer Module (Dual-Band)
notes: Returns its load and LEDs to their states before a power outage.
Its owner's manual describes linking it only as a responder.

devices.description: A controller for dimmable lighting ballasts that use a 0-10 VDC control input. It also has two relay outputs that can switch non-dimmable ballasts of up to 5 amps each.
devices.name: 0-10V Ballast Dimmer
notes: HouseLinc names it Insteon Ballast Dimmer.
Drives a 0-10V output and two relayed loads; on cmd1 0x11 or 0x13, cmd2 0x01 selects load 1, 0x02 load 2 and 0x03 both.
Turns on at 100% at power-up.
A change on an input can also change the load, using the on mask, on-level and ramp rate stored for groups 2 to 5, one for each of the four transitions.
The inputs came with a firmware update, so some versions may not send to groups 2 to 4.
Closing input 1 sends group 1, opening it group 2, closing input 2 group 3 and opening it group 4.

devices.description: A module installed inside a ceiling fan's canopy that controls the fan speed (low, medium, high) and the fan's light kit. It can be controlled by other Insteon devices or the Hub.
devices.name: Ceiling Fan and Light Control Module
notes: It takes a standard On for the light, and an extended On with 0x02 in D1 for the fan.

devices.name: In-Line On/Off Module
notes: Linked by holding SET for 10 seconds.

devices.name: On/Off Switch with Sense
notes: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008) lists 0x02/0x15 as model 2476S2.
HouseLinc lists 0x02/0x15 under 2476S.
sources: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008)

devices.name: On/Off Switch with Countdown Timer
notes: When its timer runs out it sends off to its group's members, unless its group control option is turned off.

devices.description: An in-wall dimmer switch that controls its light locally and can be controlled remotely by Insteon keypads, remotes, sensors, or the Hub. It is rated for up to 150 W of LED or 600 W of incandescent lighting.
devices.name: Dimmer Switch
notes: The 2015 owner's manual for the 2477S, 2477D and 2477DH prints subcategory 0x00, a template value; Insteon Device Categories (January 2014) gives the 2477D 0x01/0x20.

devices.description: A higher-capacity version of the Insteon wall dimmer switch, rated for up to 250 W of dimmable LED or 1,000 W of incandescent or halogen lighting. It can be controlled locally or remotely over Insteon.
devices.name: Dimmer Switch (High Wattage)
notes: Its owner's manual prints subcategory 0x20, the 2477D's; Insteon Device Categories (January 2014) gives the 2477DH 0x01/0x2D for every revision.

devices.description: An in-wall on/off switch for non-dimmable loads such as fluorescent lights, ceiling fans, and exhaust fans, rated up to 17 amps. It can be controlled locally or remotely over Insteon.
devices.name: On/Off Switch
Dimmer Switch 240V
notes: Returns its load and LEDs to their states before a power outage.

devices.name: Countdown Timer Dimmer Keypad, 8 Buttons
notes: Buttons A to H start 2, 5, 10, 15 and 30 minute and 1 and 2 hour timers, and turn the load off.
Turns its load off for a second a minute before a timer ends, unless that's turned off.
Has one ALL-Link group.

devices.name: Dimmer Keypad, 6 Buttons
notes: Each button other than the load's can be set to toggle, send only off, or send only on.
Group 1 is the On and Off buttons, which control the load. In the 8-button layout, which software can set, groups 1 to 8 are buttons A to H.
Group 9 controls the load only while it's detached from group 1.

devices.name: Dimmer Keypad, 8 Buttons
notes: Each button other than the load's can be set to toggle, send only off, or send only on.
Group 1 is button A, which controls the load. In the 6-button layout, which software can set, group 1 is the On and Off buttons and groups 3 to 6 are buttons A to D.
Group 9 controls the load only while it's detached from group 1.

devices.name: On/Off Keypad, 6 Buttons
notes: Group 1 is the On and Off buttons, which control the load. In the 8-button layout, which software can set, groups 1 to 8 are buttons A to H.
Group 9 controls the load only while it's detached from group 1.

devices.description: A wall keypad that switches its connected light fixture on and off and adds extra buttons for controlling other Insteon devices or scenes. It replaces a standard wall switch. Insteon sells it in a 6-button version.
devices.name: On/Off Keypad
notes: HouseLinc also lists its identity under 2487S-50.
Group 1 is the On and Off buttons, which control the load. In the 8-button layout, which software can set, groups 1 to 8 are buttons A to H.
Group 9 controls the load only while it's detached from group 1.

devices.name: Integrated Remote Control Thermostat
notes: A Venstar thermostat with the 2441V's board built in, so it uses the same commands.

devices.name: Dimmer Module
notes: Insteon's list of code bases puts subcategory 0x0B on the older LampLinc code base; the Global Line Developer Notes list it as the French 2632-422, with the same commands as the others.
The 2632-452, sold in Chile, reports 0x01/0x50.

devices.name: On/Off Module
notes: The 2633-452, sold in Chile on 915 MHz, reports 0x02/0x3A.

devices.description: A weather-resistant plug-in relay module for switching outdoor lights and appliances on and off remotely. It is rated NEMA 3R and works from -4 to 122 degrees Fahrenheit.
devices.name: Outdoor On/Off Plug
notes: Has no X10.
The Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes give its identity as category 0x01 and subcategory 0x3A, which the catalog gives to the 2672.
Its owner's manual lists it as an Insteon controller; its Developer Notes list it as a responder only, as the catalog does.
sources: Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes

devices.description: A plug-in relay module that switches lamps, fans, space heaters, and other small appliances on and off remotely. It handles loads of up to 15 amps or 1,800 W.
devices.name: On/Off Plug

devices.description: An in-wall duplex outlet with two receptacles that can each be switched on and off independently over Insteon. It is used to control plug-in lamps, fans, and small appliances.
devices.name: Dual On/Off Outlet
notes: Both outlets are switched, each by its own group.
An August 2014 owner's manual prints subcategory 0x29, the 2476ST's; the December 2014 manual gives 0x39.

devices.name: LED Bulb A19
notes: Has no buttons or LED.
Can be set to turn on when power returns; that's off by default.
Sold as the 2672-222 in the US, the 2672-422 (E27) and 2672-432 (B22) in Europe, and the 2672-522 (E27) and 2672-532 (B22) in Australia and New Zealand.

devices.name: LED Bulb PAR38
notes: Has no buttons or LED.

devices.name: Thermostat for Heat Pump
notes: The 2441TH's hardware with heat pump firmware, which works like the 2441TH.
HouseLinc labels subcategories 0x13 to 0x15 as 2732-232, 2732-432 and 2732-532; the Thermostat 2441TH Owner's Manual calls them 2732-242, 2732-442 and 2732-542.
Insteon Device Categories (January 2014) gives 2732-432 and 2732-532 to the Zone Thermostat, 0x05/0x11 and 0x05/0x12.

devices.name: Motorized Shades
notes: On opens and off closes; fast on and fast off open and close fully; brighten and dim start opening and closing, and stopping ends the movement.
Doesn't repeat Insteon messages.

devices.name: ICON PowerLinc Serial
sources: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008)

devices.name: ICON PowerLinc USB
sources: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008)

devices.name: I/O Module
notes: Each relay's momentary time can be set from 0.2 seconds to 100 minutes.

devices.description: A wireless, battery-powered motion sensor that sends on when it detects motion and off when the motion has stopped.
devices.name: Motion Sensor
notes: HouseLinc also lists its US identity under the 2420M.
Its heartbeat's cmd1, 0x11 to 0x14, gives the battery level from fully charged to almost empty.

devices.description: A wireless, battery-powered sensor that mounts on a door or window and reports when it opens or closes. It can switch Insteon lights or, with the Hub, send phone alerts.
devices.name: Open/Close Sensor
notes: HouseLinc lists subcategory 0x09 as the Door Sensor 2843-232.
Its heartbeat's cmd1 is 0x11 while it's open and 0x13 while it's closed.
Its Developer Notes give the heartbeat as about once every 24 hours; other sources give 23.8 hours.

With its jumper removed, in multi-scene mode, the sensor sends group 1 when it opens and group 2 when it closes. Later units without a jumper, as the 2016 Open/Close Sensor 2843 Owner's Manual describes them, have no multi-scene mode.

devices.description: A wireless, battery-powered motion sensor that can turn Insteon-controlled lights on when someone enters a room and off after they leave.
devices.name: Motion Sensor II
notes: Groups other than 1 are off by default.
Its heartbeat's cmd1, 0x11 to 0x14, gives the battery level from fully charged to almost empty.
Optional groups report temperature and light levels.

Groups 5, 6, 9 and 10 report the end of motion, dawn, heat and cold as an on instead of an off to groups 1, 2, 7 and 8; the Motion Sensor III sends to them only when they have links. Groups 7 to 10 are the Motion Sensor III's.
Its heartbeat is about once a day, plus or minus 10 percent.

devices.description: A wireless, battery-powered sensor recessed into a door frame that reports when the door opens or closes. It can trigger lights and other Insteon devices.
devices.name: Hidden Door Sensor
notes: Sends closed to group 2 only when set to.
Sends a heartbeat to group 4 every 24 hours by default. Software can set it to 5 to 1275 minutes, in 5-minute steps.
Sends low battery to group 3 each time it wakes while its battery is below a level software sets.
Sends low battery and heartbeat only when it has links in those groups.
Its heartbeat and low battery messages carry cmd1 0x11 while the door is open and 0x13 while it's closed.
Its Developer Notes give the heartbeat as every 24 hours by default; other sources give 256 times 5 minutes, about 21 hours.
Its owner's manual says the sensor sends its heartbeat once every 24 hours by default.

devices.description: A battery-powered sensor placed on the floor near sinks, toilets, washing machines, or water heaters that signals when it detects water. With an Insteon Hub or siren it can send alerts.
devices.name: Leak Sensor
notes: Its heartbeat sends on when dry and off when wet.
Once wet, it ignores further changes until its SET button is pressed.
It sends dry to group 1 only when its SET button is pressed while it's dry. It sends wet to group 2 when it detects water, or when its SET button is pressed while it's wet.
Its Developer Notes give the heartbeat as about once every 24 hours; other sources give 23.8 hours.

devices.name: ICON Dimmer Module
notes: HouseLinc and Insteon Device Categories (January 2014) also list its identity under 2856D2B; Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008) gives 2856D2.
sources: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008)

devices.name: ICON Appliance Module
notes: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008) names it the Icon Appliance Adapter.
HouseLinc lists 0x02/0x0C under 2856S3B.
sources: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008)

devices.name: ICON Appliance Module
notes: HouseLinc also lists 0x02/0x0C, which Insteon Device Categories (January 2014) gives to the 2856S3, under 2856S3B.

devices.name: Deadbolt
notes: It's asleep most of the time, so it may take a few seconds to answer a command.

devices.name: ICON Dimmer Switch
notes: Insteon Device Categories (January 2014) lists 0x01/0x03 and 0x01/0x1E as model 2876DB; Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008) gives 0x01/0x03 as 2876D.
sources: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008)

devices.name: ICON In-Wall Controller
sources: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008)

devices.name: Smoke Bridge
notes: HouseLinc names it Smoke Detector.
It sends Insteon messages over powerline only; its radio only listens for the smoke alarms it's paired with.
Tapping its SET button sends each group's command as a test, ending with the all-clear.
It sends a heartbeat to group 0x0A about once every 24 hours, which software can turn off.
Group 4 is the all-clear on earlier firmware and a new or unknown alarm on later firmware.

devices.name: Range Extender
notes: Repeats Insteon messages between powerline and RF, and bridges the two powerline phases.
Answers status requests and beeps; it has no load to control.

devices.name: Wall Keypad Switch 277V
notes: In the 8-button layout groups 1 to 8 are buttons A to H, and in the 6-button layout group 1 is the On and Off buttons and groups 3 to 6 are buttons A to D. Software sets the layout, and Insteon's documents don't say which one it ships with.

devices.name: Wall Keypad Dimmer
notes: In the 8-button layout groups 1 to 8 are buttons A to H, and in the 6-button layout group 1 is the On and Off buttons and groups 3 to 6 are buttons A to D. Software sets the layout, and Insteon's documents don't say which one it ships with.

devices.name: Wall Keypad Switch
notes: In the 8-button layout groups 1 to 8 are buttons A to H, and in the 6-button layout group 1 is the On and Off buttons and groups 3 to 6 are buttons A to D. Software sets the layout, and Insteon's documents don't say which one it ships with.
